subject: forensic-medicine
title: Plant and animal poisons: key Indian forensic facts

steps.tx: Plant and animal poisons are common in Indian medicolegal practice. Think of the **active principle** of each agent and its typical clinical picture. Snakes are the most important animal group. Venoms are grouped as **neurotoxic** (cobra, krait, coral snake), **haemotoxic** (vipers) and **myotoxic** (sea snakes). Elapids act mainly on the nervous system, causing paralysis, while vipers cause bleeding and local tissue damage.
steps.say: Plant and animal poisons are common in Indian medicolegal practice. Think of the active principle of each agent and its typical clinical picture. steps.tx: Anti snake venom (ASV) is the key treatment. Polyvalent ASV works best within **four hours** of the bite and is of doubtful value after 24 hours. Give a **test dose** first to detect hypersensitivity, then the full dose. Initial dose depends on severity: minimal envenoming needs about 5 vials, moderate about 10 vials and severe 10 to 15 vials. In neurotoxic bites a second dose is given after one hour.

steps.tx: Anti snake venom is effective for the common cobra, Russell's viper, saw-scaled viper and krait. It is **not** effective for pit vipers. Cobra venom is neurotoxic, and atropine premedication is used before neostigmine in cobra envenoming. Hypersensitivity to ASV must be checked before full dosing. Remember that elapids are in the family Elapidae, while pit vipers belong to Crotalidae.

steps.tx: Strychnine is a **spinal poison** that blocks glycine inhibition in the anterior horn cells. Convulsions affect all muscles at the same time, are precipitated by slight stimuli, and are clonic at first, later tonic. The body typically arches in **opisthotonus**. Consciousness stays clear. Preserve the brain and spinal cord with the viscera in suspected cases. The antidote is short-acting barbiturates, and the first step is control of convulsions in a dark room.

steps.tx: The image shows **strychnine** poisoning with the body arched in **opisthotonus** while consciousness stays clear. Strychnine blocks **glycine** inhibition in the anterior horn cells, so slight stimuli trigger convulsions affecting all muscles at the same time. The inset shows the Renshaw pathway where blocked inhibition leaves the motor neuron overexcited. Control convulsions first in a dark room with short acting barbiturates.
steps.say: Study the arched posture called opisthotonus. In strychnine poisoning the patient stays fully conscious while reflex convulsions grip all muscles at the same time, often set off by slight stimuli. The diagram shows why. Blocked glycine signaling removes normal inhibition in the spinal cord, so motor neurons fire out of control. Nurse the patient in a dark room and control the convulsions first.

steps.tx: The anticholinergic group, from **Datura**, belladonna and hyoscyamus, produces a classic picture: dry mouth, flushed skin, dilated pupils, hyperpyrexia and delirium. Carphologia, the picking of imaginary threads, is typical. **Physostigmine** is the effective antidote for severe anticholinergic poisoning. Mushroom poisoning from muscarine is treated with atropine instead. Hippus is classically linked with aconite.
